title: Finite-support multi-character Duhamel remainder
question: Does the exact finite Gibbs-isometric Duhamel remainder theorem combine with the EXP-001071 static finite-support envelope to give an explicit remainder bound for a fixed finite-support configuration character?

model.scope: Registered finite periodic Q3 volumes at fixed beta, compact sources, a fixed finite support S and real configuration-character amplitudes; no products, split histories, arbitrary boundaries or thermodynamic promotion.
model.finite_theorem: R_t(X)=integral_0^t (t-s) alpha_s(delta_H^2(X)) ds and Gibbs isometry gives N_beta(R_t(X))<=t^2*N_beta(delta_H^2(X))/2 for each finite Gibbs member.
model.static_input: EXP-001071 supplies N_rho(delta_H^2(W_aS))^2<=B_static_multi for the declared finite support and amplitude fixture.
model.uniformity: The displayed remainder bound is uniform only over the registered finite periodic static family with the declared support and amplitudes; it is not a support-uniform product-class estimate.

scope.not_closed: This package closes only a finite-support finite-periodic Duhamel remainder estimate. It does not establish a support-uniform product class, split-history factorial bound, direct D or delta-D Cauchy theorem, exhaustion-independent dynamics, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

Squaring the t^2/2 estimate gives t^4/4; both the factor and the reduced rational remainder are recomputed.

The support and amplitudes remain fixed at the declared fixture; no support-uniform product claim is inferred.
The finite theorem is applied per registered orientation; no plus/minus Gibbs carrier identification is asserted.
Uniformity is restricted to the registered periodic compact-source family and fixed finite support.
R254 checks rational time scaling, the unreduced/reduced envelope equality and the strict smallness bound only.
Direct D/delta-D Cauchy, product/core density, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
